title: Tetrameric Fluorescent Antigen Arrays for Single-Step Identification of Antigen-Specific B Cells
protocol: Functionalize unmodified antigen with an alkyne handle.
Add 1 equivalent of insulin (100 mg, 17.4 μmol) to a vial with DMSO (2 mL).
Dissolve the insulin by gently heating the solution to 40-50°C.
Add 1,1,3,3-tetramethylguanidine (40.2 mg, 348.8 μmol) and 1.35 equivalents of freshly prepared propargyl NHS-ester stock solution in DMSO (0.3 mL).
Stir the mixture for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Quench the reaction with 0.05% HCl (12 mL).
Purify the singly modified insulin-alkyne by reverse-phase liquid chromatography using a C18 column and a gradient of 30-40% B over 10 minutes, at a flow rate of 14 mL/min.
Evaporate acetonitrile and TFA from the eluted product using nitrogen gas or rotary evaporation under reduced pressure (650 Pascals).
Freeze the aqueous solution and lyophilize to dryness.
Store functionalized insulin at -20°C under a dry atmosphere.
Synthesize the antigen array by copper-catalyzed, azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC).
Add 38 mg of insulin-alkyne to a glass vial and dissolve in DMSO with gentle heating.
Add 50 mM sodium phosphate buffer pH 7.4 to the solution.
Add 21 mg of 20 kDa 4-arm PEG azide, copper (II) sulfate pentahydrate, Tris(3-hydroxypropyltriazolylmethyl)amine, and sodium ascorbate to the vial.
Stir for 2 h at room temperature.
Add DMSO to solubilize any precipitates.
Acidify the solution with 0.05% HCl.
Purify the antigen array by reverse-phase liquid chromatography using a preparative C18 column with a 20–60% B gradient for 10 min and flow rate of 14 ml/min.
Evaporate acetonitrile from the solution.
Freeze the aqueous solution and lyophilize to dryness.
Store the antigen array at -20 °C under a dry atmosphere.
Conjugate the fluorophore to the antigen array for 2.5 hours.
Dissolve 1 equivalent tetravalent insulin (21.7 mg, 0.5 μmol) in DMSO (1.75 mL) with gentle heating.
Add freshly prepared 100 mM carbonate buffer (8 mL), pH 9.0, to the solution.
Add 5 equivalents of fluorescein isothiocyanate in a freshly prepared 10 mM stock solution in DMSO (0.25 ml, 0.97 mg, 2.5 μmol) and stir for 2 hours in the dark at room temperature.
Purify the product by dialysis using 3.5 kDa molecular weight cutoff dialysis tubing in a stirred 5 L bucket with distilled water in the dark at room temperature.
Dialyze for 24 hours, changing the dialysis solution every 6 to 12 hours.
Freeze the dialyzed solution and lyophilize to dryness to yield the FAA.
Store the FAA in the dark under a dry atmosphere at -20°C.
Analyze the products by sodium dodecyl sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis.
Prepare samples containing 5 μg of purified monovalent antigen, 20 kDa 4-arm PEG azide, antigen array, and FAA for analysis.
Visualize fluorophore labeling in the FAA samples using fluorescence imaging in a gel-imager.
Perform Coomassie blue staining to visualize the antigen.
Perform iodine staining to visualize the PEG backbone.
Rinse the gel in distilled water for 3 x 2 min.
Incubate in a 5% barium chloride solution (20 mL) for 10 min.
Rinse the gel in distilled water for 3 x 2 min.
Incubate in a 0.1 N iodine solution (20 mL) for 1 min.
Rinse the gel in distilled water for 3 x 2 min to remove background staining.
Prepare 0.1 N iodine solution by adding potassium iodide (2.0 g, 12 mmol) and iodine (1.27 g, 5 mmol) to 100 mL of distilled water.
Dissolve a small amount of FAA at 0.1 mg/mL.
Record the absorbance at 280 nm for the FAA solution.
Measure the peak absorption wavelength for the dye.
Calculate the molar extinction coefficients for the antigen and the dye.
Perform UV-Vis spectroscopy to calculate the degree of dye-labeling.
Use an appropriately buffered solution like a 100 mM carbonate buffer with pH 8.3 when measuring the FAA absorbance.
Calculate the correction factor (CF) using the formula: CF = ADye,280 nm / (ADye,maxλ * 0.25 * (ADye,maxλ / EDye,maxλ) * (Eantigen,280 nm / (A280 nm – (ADye,maxλ * CF))))
Analyze the FAA for free dye or potential degradation products by RP-HPLC.
Dissolve a small amount of FAA at 1.0 mg/mL.
Analyze with an analytical C18 column (4.6 mm x 150 mm, 300 A pore size, 2.5 μm particle size).
Use a 10 min 5–95% B gradient (A, water with 0.05% trifluoroacetic acid: B, acetonitrile with 0.05% trifluoroacetic acid) with a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Set the UV-Vis detector to monitor the peak absorbance wavelength of the dye at 437 nm for FITC.
Suspend FAA stock to 1 mg/mL in FACS buffer (1x PBS + 5% fetal bovine serum and 0.1% sodium azide).
Consider incorporating up to 10% DMSO to accelerate dissolution.
Obtain cells positive for antigen-specific B cells and dispense into microcentrifuge tubes.
Dispense 5 x 10^5 cells for titration labeling replicates.
Dispense 1 x 10^5 cells for single-stain controls as well as an unstained control.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge at 200 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend cell pellets in 50 μL of FACS buffer.
Add CD3 and CD19 fluorescent antibodies to each sample at manufacturer recommended concentrations.
Add titrated FAA doses.
Mix each sample well and incubate covered from light, on ice for 30 min.
After the incubation, wash cells by adding 1 mL of FACS buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge the samples at 200 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge the samples at 200 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the samples in 200 µL of fresh FACS buffer.
Place the samples on ice and head to the cytometer.
Run the samples on the cytometer.
Collect at least 50,000 events.
